questions.question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

Statements:

All kites are eagles.

All eagles are birds.

Conclusions:

(I) All birds are kites.

(II) Some birds are eagles.
questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as shown below :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ccf2c024f17bc2f4823a90caf261343ae189fdfc9b632f2eeee2c63f457a1b1e.png] 

Conclusions:

(I) All birds are kites → Does not follow (As all kites are eagles and all eagles are birds. So it is possible but not definite)

(II) Some birds are eagles → **F**ollow (As all eagles are birds. As whole eagles comes in birds, therefore it is true.)

∴ Here, Only conclusion (II) follows.​

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 4"

questions.question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

Statements:

Some horses are goats.

All goats are jackals.

Conclusions:

(I): Some horses are jackals.

(II): All jackals are goats.
questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as shown below :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/575612b8dda7e2bd41c77e9e0865a54ba0a4f02fca4ffc2228486e8e47dfd61a.png]

(II): All jackals are goats → Does not follow (As all goats are jackals. So it is possible but not definite)

∴ Here, Only conclusion (I) follows.​

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 1".

questions.question:
A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). Only three people sit between E and F when counted from the left of E. Only three people sit between G and D when counted from the right of D. A sits to the immediate right of G. C is an immediate neighbour of D as well as F.

Who sits second to the left of B?
questions.solution:
Given: A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table facing the centre.

1) Only three people sit between G and D when counted from the right of D. 

2) A sits to the immediate right of G. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/dc2e1eebeaf8e279190c39afeeb48b02a4c52e9353fafc7672b27608ba52dc81.png] 

3) C is an immediate neighbour of D as well as F.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/31b94b6033b17d3e7cd9e41319cb26d5b5e721d355b3977ddbb83e8ae2a946d8.png] 

4) Only three people sit between E and F when counted from the left of E. 

After positioning E only one position is left which will be occupied by the only person left i.e. B.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/45ff4c1f27129902eee70dfc5266e9ad62748cf4f7890b94362b01c93e501014.png] 

Thus, according to the final arrangement C sits second to the left of B.

Hence, "Option 2" is the correct answer.
